people.name: Chao-Ju (Jennifer) Hou

website.source_note: Wikipedia article (no personal or institutional page found live)

people.current_position: Deceased (died December 2, 2007); was Professor of Computer Science, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign

bio.summary: Chao-Ju Jennifer Hou (1964-2007) was a Taiwanese computer scientist and electrical engineer specializing in wireless sensor networks. Hou earned a BS from National Taiwan University (1987) and an MS (1989), a second MS in industrial and operations engineering (1991) and a PhD (1993) from the University of Michigan. Hou was on the faculty at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1993), Ohio State University (1996), and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (2001), where Hou directed the INDEX group. Hou was posthumously named an IEEE Fellow in 2008.
research_areas: wireless network protocol design and analysis
notable: IEEE Fellow (2008, posthumous): for contributions to protocol design and analysis of wireless communications networks
Director, Illinois Network Design and Experimentation (INDEX) group

people.notes: Wikipedia used for bio and website. No photo found on an embeddable page (Wikipedia has no image; UIUC INDEX page not reachable). Students already in tree not re-listed; could not access a complete student list (search budget exhausted), so no new students reported.

people.name: David J. Musliner (co-advised with Ed Durfee)

bio.summary: David Musliner is a Fellow at Smart Information Flow Technologies (SIFT) with over twenty-five years of research in intelligent systems, including planning and control for autonomous systems, formal verification and autonomous cyber security. For the PhD dissertation, Musliner designed the Cooperative Intelligent Real-Time Control Architecture (CIRCA), an AI planning and control architecture for hard real-time domains with safety guarantees. Musliner led SIFT's team in the DARPA Cyber Grand Challenge (FuzzBOMB).
bio.thesis_title: CIRCA: A Cooperative Approach to Intelligent Real-Time Control Architecture
notable: Led DARPA-funded FuzzBuster and CIRCADIA projects
SIFT team lead, DARPA Cyber Grand Challenge (FuzzBOMB)
Co-inventor on US patent on incremental verification

people.notes: SIFT staff page used for website, photo, bio; mathgenealogy confirms thesis and co-advisors Durfee and Shin. No PhD students found (industry researcher; not searched exhaustively).
